Publisher captions contain Thank you and punctuation cues during introductory/outro credits; those artifacts are excluded from the teaching spine. Their endpoints alone do not certify speech coverage.
Publisher captions as well as ASR can corrupt formula factors. Handwritten recording frames and primary mathematics establish the equations.
ASR calls Moran moron and misrecognizes some probability factors; handwritten frames and publisher captions resolve these.
Occasional spoken type-label swaps are resolved to mutant B and resident A consistently.
A verbal assertion of certain deleterious-mutant elimination is corrected for finite positive-fitness models.
A million origins per expected neutral fixation is an expectation, not an exact count or guaranteed success.
Sampled recording frames support formulas; no claim of full frame-by-frame visual review.

sections.section: A successful lineage must survive its first few replacements
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Chance versus selection; marked cell in chemostat; fixation question; no new mutation.
sections.teaching_construction: Five-cell marked-strain running case; explicit distinction between census and fixed-size idealization; correction of deterministic deleterious-loss claim.

sections.section: One parent and one replacement determine the next count
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: State i, N-i resident count, paired birth/loss, fitness-weighted parent probabilities, upward/downward transitions.
sections.teaching_construction: Normalized relative fitness r=R_B/R_A; stable mutant B/resident A notation; four-outcome table and rational finite example.

sections.section: No change is a real event, with a real probability
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Two same-type replacements; exhaustive four cases; normalization to one.
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit independent replacement rule, self-loops and count-change clock distinction.

sections.section: The interior states are temporary, even when the next step is uncertain
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Number line, N+1 states, steps of size zero or one, endpoints versus fluctuating interior states.
sections.teaching_construction: Positive-path finite-block proof of almost-sure absorption and finite expected absorption time.

sections.section: A probability over complete histories satisfies a one-step equation
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Fixation variable, endpoints zero and one, first-step conditioning recurrence.
sections.teaching_construction: Translation of recording x_i to u_i; local probability versus eventual probability; five-cell neutral check.

sections.section: The boundary values make the linear system determinate
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Interdependent interior equations, simultaneous system and fixed boundary values.
sections.teaching_construction: Tridiagonal structure, discrete maximum-principle uniqueness proof and checked finite vector.

sections.section: Neutrality makes fixation proportional to the starting count
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Equal-lineage symmetry, one-copy 1/N, general i/N and neutral assumptions.
sections.teaching_construction: Explicit increment proof, several initial marked cells, census/effective-size boundary.

sections.section: No directional drift does not mean no evolutionary change
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Loss versus fixation probability; many neutral origins lost; million-cell illustrative probability.
sections.teaching_construction: Conditional drift/variance, independent restarted-trial probability, distinction between expectation and certainty, rare-origin mutation-supply extension.

sections.section: Neutrality makes fixation proportional to the starting count: transition check
sections.timing_source: local machine transcription, reconciled with publisher captions and recording frames; both raw sources retained privately
sections.lecture_material: Substitution of equal fitness into both upward/downward probability formulas.
sections.teaching_construction: Neutral transition formulas integrated into neutral derivation rather than repeated as an unconnected section.

sections.lecture_material: No additional selected-case derivation attributed to lectures32–35.
sections.research_extension: Kluth and Baake section2 PDF pages2–3 finite Moran fixation sum; Kimura printed pp715–716 model-specific diffusion comparison.
sections.teaching_construction: General positive-r increments proof, beneficial/deleterious rational checks, order of limits and time-clock translation.
sections.evidence_class: original theorem derivation and verified primary-source comparison

sections.section: Absorption time, independent finite solver, six exercises and model limits
sections.research_extension: None required for original finite derivations.
sections.teaching_construction: Expected event-time recurrence, neutral harmonic-sum proof, exact Fraction linear solver, varied fully reasoned solutions and assay limitations.

references.title: Kluth and Baake, The Moran model with selection (2013)
references.supports: Fixed haploid population, uniform replacement, continuous-time birth/death rates and finite fixation sum. Section2 PDF pages2–3; time convention explicitly translated.

references.title: Kimura, On the Probability of Fixation of Mutant Genes in a Population (1962)
references.supports: Diffusion assumptions and diploid genic selection/offspring-variance convention underlying the small-s 2s limit. Printed pp713–716, especially715–716.
